note: Synthetic sources written for this template's test runs. None is a real publication or video.
topic: Portfolio optimisation methods for combining a few trading strategies

sources.title: Equal weight is hard to beat
sources.abstract: Across 14 strategy books from 2000 to 2020, mean-variance weights estimated on five years of data underperformed equal weights out of sample. Estimation error in expected returns explained most of the gap.

sources.title: Shrinking the covariance matrix
sources.abstract: Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage of the covariance matrix cut out-of-sample portfolio volatility by 12% against the sample covariance. Gains were largest when the number of assets was close to the length of the history.

sources.title: Risk parity for strategy books
sources.abstract: Weighting strategies by inverse volatility gave a higher Sharpe ratio than equal weights in 9 of 12 books. The paper uses no transaction costs.

sources.title: Hierarchical risk parity out of sample
sources.abstract: Hierarchical risk parity matched minimum variance on volatility and beat it on turnover in a 2005 to 2022 out-of-sample test. It did not beat equal weights on Sharpe ratio after costs.

sources.title: Black-Litterman views for a quant desk
sources.abstract: Blending equilibrium returns with desk views gave stable weights. The note reports no backtest.

sources.title: CVaR optimisation for fat tails
sources.abstract: Minimising conditional value at risk at the 95% level reduced the worst month by a third against mean-variance in simulated fat-tailed returns. Results on real strategy returns are left for future work.

sources.title: I tried risk parity on my bots
sources.abstract: The creator shows a backtest where inverse-volatility weights on four bots smoothed the equity curve from 2019 to 2023. Costs are not shown.

sources.title: Why Kelly sizing wins
sources.abstract: The creator claims full Kelly weights double returns for any book. No backtest is shown.

sources.title: Turnover costs of optimised weights
sources.abstract: Monthly rebalanced mean-variance weights paid 1.8% a year in costs, which erased their in-sample edge. Imposing turnover limits recovered half of it.

sources.title: Regime-aware weights
sources.abstract: Switching between two weight sets by a volatility regime raised the Sharpe ratio from 0.7 to 0.8 in sample. No out-of-sample test is reported.

sources.title: Correlation spikes in crises
sources.abstract: Strategy correlations rose towards one in the 2008 and 2020 sell-offs, so diversification fell when it was needed most.

sources.title: Minimum variance with constraints
sources.abstract: Long-only minimum variance with a 30% cap per strategy had lower drawdowns than equal weights in a 2000 to 2021 out-of-sample test, with similar Sharpe ratio.
